title: Angle Relationships
subtitle: Complementary, Supplementary, Vertical
bounds: Angles in tens. Every given, unknown and answer angle is a multiple of 10 from 10 to 180 degrees (an x is 10 to 170 on its own, as in x + 40, and 10 to 90 once it has a coefficient). Every + and − on angles is a tens fact (180 − 70 is 18 − 7): operands and results 1-18 tens. Every × and ÷ is a times-table fact in tens: coefficients 1-9, a divisor 2-9 into 18 tens or less (3x = 180 is 18 ÷ 3), a quotient 1-9 tens. Totals are only a right angle (90) and a straight line (180). Angles stay in tens: no half-angles, no angles around a point (360), no triangle sum, no parallel lines. Choices are plain numbers (or the words Complementary, Supplementary, Vertical, Adjacent, Equal); wrong choices are whatever a misreading gives (65, 12, 350), up to 999.

tiers.name: Complement & Supplement
tiers.description: Find the angle that adds to 90 (complement) or to 180 (supplement).

tiers.name: Vertical & Adjacent
tiers.description: Two lines cross: vertical angles are equal, angles next to each other add to 180.

tiers.name: Name It & Split Angles
tiers.description: Name the angle pairs, then find the missing part of a right angle or a straight line.

tiers.name: Solve for the Angle
tiers.description: Angle pairs with x in them: write the equation and solve for x.

tiers.name: Multi-Step Angles
tiers.description: Vertical and adjacent angles with 2x + 10 style expressions; find x or the angle.

COMP_SUPP_SWAP.student: Complementary adds to 90 (a corner). Supplementary adds to 180 (a line).
COMP_SUPP_SWAP.teacher: Swaps the totals: uses 180 for a complement or 90 for a supplement (or swaps the two words).

USED_360.student: A right angle is 90 and a straight line is 180. 360 is a full turn.
USED_360.teacher: Subtracts from 360 (a full turn) instead of 90 or 180.

ADDED_NOT_SUB.student: The other angle is what is left of the total. Subtract, don't add.
ADDED_NOT_SUB.teacher: Adds the given angle to the total (30 + 90) instead of subtracting it.

SUPP_FOR_VERT.student: Vertical angles are equal. Supplementary angles are the ones that add to 180.
SUPP_FOR_VERT.teacher: Treats vertical angles as supplementary: gives 180 minus the angle instead of the same angle.

COMP_FOR_VERT.student: Vertical angles are equal. Complementary angles are the ones that add to 90.
COMP_FOR_VERT.teacher: Treats vertical angles as complementary: gives 90 minus the angle (or its distance from 90) instead of the same angle.

VERT_FOR_ADJ.student: Angles next to each other on a line add to 180. They are not equal.
VERT_FOR_ADJ.teacher: Treats adjacent angles on a line as equal (vertical): gives the same angle instead of 180 minus it.

COMP_FOR_SUPP.student: A straight line is 180 degrees, not 90. Angles on a line add to 180.
COMP_FOR_SUPP.teacher: Uses 90 (a right angle) as the total for angles on a straight line: 90 minus the angle (or its distance from 90).

POSITION_WORD_FOR_SUM.student: Look at the sum: 90 is complementary, 180 is supplementary.
POSITION_WORD_FOR_SUM.teacher: Names a pair by position (vertical) when the clue is the sum they add to.

SUM_WORD_FOR_POSITION.student: Vertical and adjacent say where angles sit, not what they add to.
SUM_WORD_FOR_POSITION.teacher: Names a pair by its sum (complementary or supplementary) when the clue is where the angles sit.

VERT_ADJ_SWAP.student: Adjacent angles share a side. Vertical angles sit across from each other.
VERT_ADJ_SWAP.teacher: Swaps vertical (across from each other, equal) and adjacent (next to each other, share a side).

FORGOT_ONE.student: Take away every angle you are given, not just one.
FORGOT_ONE.teacher: Subtracts only one of the given angles (or leaves out the +number on x).

WRONG_TOTAL.student: A right angle is 90 degrees. A straight line is 180. Use the right total.
WRONG_TOTAL.teacher: Uses 180 for a right angle or 90 for a straight line.

ADDED_PARTS.student: x is what is left. Subtract the given angles from the total, don't add.
ADDED_PARTS.teacher: Adds the given angles instead of subtracting them from the total.

ANGLE_NOT_X.student: Check what is asked: here you want x, not the size of an angle.
ANGLE_NOT_X.teacher: Finds an angle's size (or copies a given angle) when the question asks for x.

NO_DIVIDE.student: You stopped early. Divide by the number in front of x.
NO_DIVIDE.teacher: Combines the terms and forgets the last step of dividing by the coefficient of x.

SPLIT_EVENLY.student: The angles are not equal. Add the parts: x + 2x is 3x, so divide by 3.
SPLIT_EVENLY.teacher: Splits the total in half as if both angles were equal, ignoring the coefficients.

SIGN_SLIP.student: A + number on one side becomes minus when it moves to the other side.
SIGN_SLIP.teacher: Moves a +number across the equals sign without changing its sign.

DIVIDED_ONE_TERM.student: Subtract the other angle first, then divide by the number in front of x.
DIVIDED_ONE_TERM.teacher: Divides only the total by the coefficient of x and leaves the other angle undivided.

GAVE_X.student: x is not the angle. Multiply x by the number in front to get the angle.
GAVE_X.teacher: Stops at the value of x when the question asks for the size of an angle.

OTHER_ANGLE.student: Re-read the question: it asks for the larger or the smaller angle.
OTHER_ANGLE.teacher: Finds the right angles but answers with the wrong one (smaller for larger, or the reverse).
